title: The binary propositional resolution rule is sound
statement: For all propositions p, q, r: if (p or q) holds and ((not p) or r) holds, then (q or r) holds.

formal.statement: (assert (=> (and (or p q) (or (not p) r)) (or q r)))

evidence.supports: For all propositions p, q, r: if (p or q) holds and ((not p) or r) holds, then (q or r) holds.
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14: the file asserts the NEGATION of formal.statement and the solver reported `unsat` with `kind=unsat-term-level certified=1 arena=ok`. `unsat-term-level` is exhaustive evaluation of the 8 Boolean assignments by the axeyum-ir evaluator alone -- it trusts neither the bit-blaster, the CNF encoder, nor the SAT solver. `arena=ok` means Evidence::check re-ran that enumeration against a FRESH PARSE of the file, independent of anything the producing solve held in memory. Independently cross-checked: `z3 -smt2` on the same file also reports `unsat`.

notes:
The one-step soundness of resolution: the rule the CDCL core in axeyum-cnf derives every learned clause with, and the rule a DRAT/RUP checker replays. This fact is the propositional shadow of the property the whole UNSAT-certificate story rests on. What it is NOT: a proof that resolution is refutation-COMPLETE, or that our learned clauses are always resolvents of asserted ones. Both are metatheorems about a proof system, and nothing in this repository can state a proof system as an object, so they are out of reach -- see F:godel-first-incompleteness for the same gap in a more famous costume.

On the axiom footprint: it names the trust base of the SMT ROUTE that established this fact -- the axeyum-ir Boolean evaluator, and the two-valued semantics of the SMT-LIB Bool sort that makes exhaustive truth-table enumeration a proof. It is deliberately NOT empty and deliberately NOT a Lean axiom list. Nothing here went through axeyum's Lean kernel. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_axiom_inventory`: the `logic` prelude reports axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0, and its declarations are exactly True, False, And, Or, Iff, Not (as `a -> False`), Eq and Exists -- an intuitionistic core with no `Classical.em`, no `propext` and no `Quot.sound`. Zero trusted declarations there means the kernel assumes nothing, not that it can prove everything.
